page.description: openSUSE Tumbleweed editions and architectures: compare, download official images, or prepare a USB with ROMinit CLI.
page.intro: openSUSE's rolling release: tested snapshot by snapshot, installed with Agama and updated with zypper dup, with KDE Plasma, GNOME or Xfce as the desktop.
pros: Rolling release with tested snapshots, not raw upstream churn.
Offline DVD and small network installers for several architectures.
YaST and zypper, with Btrfs snapshots and rollback by default.
cons: Snapshot updates arrive often and need a reboot cycle.
The rolling model expects regular maintenance.
i686 images are still offered although the installer guide says 32-bit CPUs are unsupported.
No long support window: Leap is the fixed-release sibling.
page.previewNote: No screenshot with a reusable licence was confirmed for openSUSE Tumbleweed; the page shows the logo only. No image was written to a USB stick and nothing was booted.
page.status: Write the offline DVD or the network installer to a USB stick and boot it; Agama partitions the target disk. Writing erases the stick, and the install erases the chosen partitions.

editions.name: Offline DVD (x86_64)
editions.description: The full offline installer with the complete package set.
editions.usbNote: 4.7 GB image. Write it with dd or any image writer; writing erases the stick.

editions.name: Network installer (x86_64)
editions.description: A small installer that downloads packages during installation.
editions.usbNote: 418 MB image. Write it with dd or any image writer; writing erases the stick, and the install needs a network connection.
